object: German mathematician (1862–1943).  Posed the 23 problems that shaped twentieth-century mathematics.  His formalization program — the attempt to ground all mathematics on a complete, consistent, decidable foundation — was the mathematical equivalent of the deterministic worldview.  Gödel destroyed it in 1931.
